evidence: Codex 0.155.1 upstream writes provider-owned state under CODEX_HOME/.tmp, including plugin-share-local-paths-v1.json and rollout-maintenance.lock. v0.4.2 admits .tmp only through the initialized-capability provider roots after CLROOM's v2 state marker exists; both a fresh uninitialized shadow and the legacy .sandbox_migration compatibility path remain unable to authorize preexisting .tmp, and unknown top-level siblings still fail closed.

Pinned Claude Code 2.1.278 includes the built-in agents-md ancestor walk introduced in Claude Code 2.1.277 for AGENTS.md and .claude/AGENTS.md. CLROOM now denies those exact files only above the nearest real Git worktree boundary (or the launch directory outside Git), preserving repo-root and nested project instructions when Claude starts from a subdirectory.

Regression coverage proves initialized .tmp provider state survives a later CLROOM launch, preexisting unowned .tmp still fails closed, real Codex qualification executes twice against one synthetic home, pre-tag whole-plugin evidence cannot be written until a post-interactive clean relaunch succeeds, and canonical readiness owns the exact-tag Draft verifier.

Release-domain classification explicitly maps scripts/probe/** to the tests domain, and the release-contract self-test includes the sitemap probe path so future probe scripts cannot silently become unclassified release delta.

macOS Seatbelt isolation coverage models a nested working directory inside a Git worktree and proves AGENTS.md and .claude/AGENTS.md above the worktree are unreadable while both repo-root and nested project variants remain readable.

Claude ancestor-instruction isolation also denies a symlinked external ancestor AGENTS.md while retaining repo-root and nested AGENTS.md/.claude/AGENTS.md, covering path-alias bypass without collapsing the project context boundary to the current directory.

The exact-artifact Claude AGENTS boundary probe launches from a nested directory beneath a synthetic .git worktree, fails if HOME/workspace ancestor AGENTS are readable, and independently fails if repo-root or nested project AGENTS become unreadable.
Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock advance only the package version to 0.4.2; no runtime or build dependency is added, removed, or replaced.

Real Codex provider qualification requires two provider observations on the same synthetic HOME and v2 evidence. The provider-canary contract itself now asserts the lifecycle-v2 smoke, two-run qualifier, tag-evidence fields and v0.4.2 negative fixture so release hardening cannot silently regress to the former v1 contract.

Public discovery verification now validates the explicit sitemap source contract in CI and, after same-SHA CI plus Pages deployment, probes the canonical published sitemap over HTTPS with redirects refused, bounded retries/size, XML parsing, canonical-host/path enforcement, duplicate rejection, and canonical-home presence before IndexNow notification.

The pre-tag helper accepts only lifecycle-aware Codex v2 evidence with a successful clean relaunch after the interactive selected-plugin TUI. A new canonical verify-draft-release.sh reconciles exact tag/SHA identity, Draft assets, checksums, attestations, current provider pins, local pre-tag/Draft evidence, and every exact-tag push Action before any publish gate; canonical readiness verifies this verifier is executable and shell-valid.

Claude pre-tag evidence advances to clroom.plugin-release-smoke.v2 and protected-tag validation requires both project_agents_retained_confirmed=true and external_ancestor_agents_absent_confirmed=true. The real pinned-provider selected-plugin TUI runs in a task-owned synthetic nested Git project, so a provider walk that drops legitimate project AGENTS or admits an external ancestor cannot authorize a tag.

The release checker now binds reviewed_through_commit to the exact candidate history: it must be an ancestor of HEAD and every tracked change after that commit must be confined to the release-review snapshot, so substantive post-review changes cannot be legalized by a digest-only reseal.

The synthetic Claude AGENTS artifact probe now proves the launched provider body executed from a nested Git working directory: version preflight alone cannot satisfy evidence, external ancestors must be denied, repo-root and nested AGENTS must remain readable, and the provider writes an execution marker only after those assertions.

The accepted-main Claude AGENTS artifact probe now makes its synthetic TMPDIR private (0700) before launch and fails closed if that mode is not retained. This matches the existing session-only projection security invariant instead of causing the probe fixture itself to fail before provider execution.

Current README and Codex/Claude/limitations documentation identify v0.4.2 as the candidate capability version, while CHANGELOG records that v0.4.1 remained an unpublished Draft candidate and that v0.4.2 supersedes it.

The published GitHub Pages sitemap is now checked end to end against the canonical y-sor.github.io/clean-room-launcher URL surface, so malformed XML, foreign-host entries, duplicates, missing canonical home, redirects, and non-XML responses fail the discovery pipeline instead of being inferred from source configuration alone.

The Claude launch plaque now reports Global AGENTS.md off, and Claude documentation describes the 2.1.278 agents-md boundary instead of implying that CLAUDE.md is the provider's only instruction surface.

near_misses.durable_control: Codex activation requires both exact-bundle projection into the active private shadow PluginStore and session-layer exact plugin enablement; session flags alone are not treated as qualification evidence.

Shadow PluginStore selection is single-bundle only, verified by path+digest ownership marker and cache-only-selected checks; stale owned projections are reconciled, while unknown siblings or tampered projections fail closed and are preserved rather than blindly deleted.

Projection preserves executable bits while removing write bits recursively; provider sandbox also write-denies the shadow plugin cache and marker, with regression tests for read-only and executable semantics.
Provider identity/version, installed source identity/digest and projected bundle are revalidated after planning and again immediately before provider exec; any drift refuses before provider birth.
When CLROOM plugin selection is active, raw Codex config/profile/feature/plugin controls are refused before provider birth; arguments after the provider terminator remain literal.

Canonical provider-pins.sh records exact current-stable versions and npm integrity; check-provider-pins.sh verifies latest tags and integrity during candidate provisioning and again at the action-time tag boundary.

Release contract tests and qualification evidence verification consume the canonical pinned provider versions instead of duplicating stale provider version/digest literals; evidence is rejected unless its provider version exactly matches the pinned canary version.
Public identity tests include features.remote_plugin=false in the exact Codex clean argv contract while preserving native Codex process identity and passthrough semantics.
The post-v0.4.0 release delta explicitly verifies the exported SBOM attestation bundle with the CycloneDX predicate before publication.

Protected-tag helper refreshes main/tag/ruleset/release-contract/provider-pin state at action time, compares local provider version and bytes to pretag evidence, performs one tag push, then reconciles the authoritative remote result.

Release readiness provisions the pinned current Codex canary before full locked tests; negative qualification tests derive the executable's actual provider version and therefore exercise the fail-closed harness instead of returning early or failing before evidence creation.

Codex v0.4.1 uses a new .clroom-clean-state-v2/.clroom-state-v2 shadow generation. Legacy v1 shadow state is preserved but never imported or deleted; regression coverage seeds stale plugin-cache content in v1 and proves selected projection starts in clean v2 state while the existing unknown-sibling guard remains fail-closed.

Codex state management and sandbox write denial consume the same shared active shadow-generation constant; regression coverage requires the sandbox profile to protect the active v2 plugin cache and not the preserved legacy v1 cache.

near_misses.failure_mode: Codex CLI dotted-path encoding can misaddress provider-owned plugin IDs, and selected whole-plugin MCP capability can remain disabled by provider MCP policy.
near_misses.durable_control: Atomic root-level exact-plugin config with MCP enablement derived only from the captured exact bundle inventory, covered by real-provider clean→selected→clean qualification.

near_misses.failure_mode: Pinned Codex 0.155.1 legitimately creates CODEX_HOME/.tmp state after CLROOM shadow initialization; the previous static allowlist rejected that state on the next launch.
near_misses.durable_control: The initialized v2 shadow admits the exact provider-owned .tmp top-level class, with regression fixtures for pinned upstream plugin-share and rollout-maintenance state plus a negative test proving preexisting unowned .tmp remains fail-closed.

near_misses.failure_mode: The v0.4.1 pre-tag smoke proved clean→selected→clean before the selected interactive TUI, then accepted evidence without proving the next clean launch after provider-written interactive state.
near_misses.durable_control: Codex pre-tag evidence schema v2 requires clean→selected→clean→selected interactive TUI→clean on the same persistent shadow; push-release-tag.sh rejects evidence without post_interactive_clean_confirmed=true.

near_misses.failure_mode: A successful Release workflow was initially treated as the relevant Draft signal while a separate exact-tag CI run had failed, so manual review could miss an independent tag-triggered blocker.
near_misses.durable_control: Canonical verify-draft-release.sh requires all exact-tag push Actions for the exact source SHA, including CI and Release, to be completed successfully and also reconciles Draft identity/assets/attestations/provider pins/local evidence before a publish verdict.

near_misses.failure_mode: The previous evidence field name persistent_provider_state_unchanged overstated what the smoke actually fingerprinted: ambient config.toml and the ambient plugin tree, while CLROOM shadow provider state is intentionally allowed to evolve.
near_misses.durable_control: Codex v2 evidence names the measured invariant ambient_config_and_plugin_tree_unchanged and separately proves provider_state_lifecycle_closed, preventing evidence semantics from claiming stronger state immutability than was measured.

near_misses.failure_mode: Source-level sitemap configuration could pass while the deployed GitHub Pages sitemap was malformed, redirected, stale, foreign-hosted, or otherwise unusable by crawlers.
near_misses.durable_control: CI validates the sitemap template and negative fixtures, while the same-SHA post-Pages IndexNow workflow fetches the canonical live sitemap with redirects refused and bounded XML/canonical-URL validation before search-engine notification.

near_misses.failure_mode: Pinned Claude Code 2.1.278 includes the built-in agents-md ancestor walk introduced in 2.1.277. The existing clean-launch model and pre-tag smoke covered CLAUDE.md/settings/skills but allowed an external ancestor AGENTS.md to enter the real selected-plugin TUI.
near_misses.durable_control: Claude isolation now denies AGENTS.md and .claude/AGENTS.md above the nearest real Git worktree boundary (or cwd outside Git), preserves repo-root and nested project instructions, and carries negative/positive sandbox, launched-provider, exact-artifact and real-TUI evidence into pre-tag schema v2 and the protected tag gate.

near_misses.failure_mode: The v0.4.2 review snapshot could carry a stale reviewed_through_commit while later substantive test/release-gate commits entered the candidate; the content digest detected tree drift but did not prove that the declared semantic review boundary actually covered those commits.
near_misses.durable_control: check-release-contract.py now requires reviewed_through_commit to be an ancestor of the exact HEAD and rejects every post-boundary tracked change except the release-review snapshot itself; contract regression coverage makes the history binding durable.

near_misses.failure_mode: The first synthetic artifact boundary probe invoked clroom claude --version while its fake provider exited successfully on the version path before testing AGENTS reads, so evidence could report PASS without executing the launched-provider isolation assertions.
near_misses.durable_control: The probe now launches the normal Claude provider path, writes a task-owned execution marker only after external-ancestor deny and project-local positive assertions execute, fails if that marker is absent, and the provider-canary contract requires the execution-marker guard.

near_misses.failure_mode: The first AGENTS isolation repair treated the launch working directory itself as the project boundary. A user starting Claude from repo/subdir would therefore lose the legitimate repo-root AGENTS.md that Claude's project instruction walk is expected to retain.
near_misses.durable_control: For Git projects the boundary is now the nearest real non-symlink .git file/directory; outside Git it falls back to the launch directory. Unit, launched-provider and exact-artifact regression probes all start from a nested cwd and require external ancestors to stay denied while repo-root plus nested AGENTS.md/.claude/AGENTS.md remain readable.

near_misses.failure_mode: A real-TUI check that confirmed only the absence of an external ancestor AGENTS.md could still pass if Claude's agents-md ancestor walk failed on the denied ambient file and consequently dropped legitimate repo-root or nested project AGENTS instructions too.
near_misses.durable_control: The pre-tag real pinned-provider TUI now runs inside a task-owned synthetic nested Git project and requires both positive project AGENTS visibility and negative external-ancestor absence. Evidence v2 records project_agents_retained_confirmed separately, and the protected tag plus pre-publish verifier require that positive proof.

near_misses.failure_mode: The accepted-main Claude AGENTS artifact probe created its synthetic TMPDIR with the caller's default umask. Under a normal 022 umask the directory became 0755, so CLROOM correctly rejected session-only projection setup before the fake provider ran, making the release gate report AGENTS_BOUNDARY_SANDBOX_PROBE without exercising the intended boundary assertions.
near_misses.durable_control: The pre-tag probe explicitly chmods its synthetic TMPDIR to 0700 and fail-closes on the observed mode before launch; the provider-canary contract statically requires both the private-TMPDIR setup and its failure marker so the fixture cannot silently regress.

near_misses.failure_mode: The installed Codex whole-plugin bundle declared its codex_app MCP launcher with absolute command/cwd paths rooted in the ambient PluginStore. CLROOM copied the bundle into its private shadow PluginStore but preserved those absolute paths, so `mcp list --json` could show the selected server while the real interactive TUI failed to start it because ambient plugin access remained correctly sandbox-denied.
near_misses.durable_control: Codex plugin projection now deterministically rebases only absolute legacy MCP command/cwd paths that resolve inside the exact selected source bundle to the corresponding shadow bundle paths, while unrelated absolute commands remain unchanged and ambient PluginStore access stays denied. Semantic source/projection digest binding, a negative reintroduced-ambient-path regression, automated selected-transport path verification, and mandatory real-TUI confirmation that codex_app is healthy/ready with tools prevent configuration visibility from being mistaken for runtime startup.

Download exact Draft Release v0.4.2 archive, verify checksums/provenance/CycloneDX bundles, prove clean→selected→clean Codex plugin behavior against the Draft bytes including selected_mcp_plugin_paths_rebased=true for the installed codex-app-tools MCP transport, and pass canonical exact-tag pre-publish reconciliation including all tag-triggered Actions and accepted local evidence.

Requalify the shipped Claude whole-plugin path on pinned current-stable Claude Code 2.1.278 using exact accepted-main v0.4.2 bytes; prove clean absence, selected presence, no newly admitted sibling, no plugin errors, unchanged persistent provider config, external-above-worktree AGENTS exclusion, repo-root and nested project AGENTS retention from a nested cwd, and a normal selected-plugin interactive TUI without a model prompt. The real TUI must run in a task-owned synthetic nested Git project and accepted v2 evidence must confirm both project_agents_retained_confirmed=true and external_ancestor_agents_absent_confirmed=true.

Re-run the Claude plugin capability smoke on exact Draft Release v0.4.2 bytes after checksum and attestation verification, bound to Claude Code 2.1.278, then include its evidence in canonical exact-tag pre-publish reconciliation.

product_outcome: Ship v0.4.2 as the bounded exact Codex whole-plugin selective-restore slice from the published v0.4.0 baseline, while repairing provider-written state lifecycle compatibility and promoting fail-closed pre-tag and pre-publish reconciliation so a successful first launch or one successful workflow cannot be mistaken for release readiness. The same candidate hardens public discovery by verifying the deployed canonical sitemap before IndexNow notification and closes Claude 2.1.278 built-in agents-md ambient-instruction drift without suppressing legitimate repo-root project instructions when launched from a nested directory. The final candidate also keeps the ambient Codex PluginStore denied while rebasing provider-authored in-bundle legacy MCP launcher paths into the exact selected shadow projection so configuration discovery and real MCP startup agree.

contract_evolution_review.rationale: The unpublished v0.4.1 Draft exposed two missing lifecycle boundaries and one review-reconciliation gap: legitimate pinned-provider state could make the next launch fail, interactive pre-tag state was not followed by a clean relaunch, and a reviewer could inspect the Release workflow while missing a separate failed exact-tag CI run. Because these are release near-misses, v0.4.2 promotes durable runtime, evidence, tag-gate, CI lifecycle, and exact-tag pre-publish reconciliation controls rather than deleting state or relying on manual vigilance. The candidate also closes a public-discovery verification gap by promoting the sitemap from source-only checks to a same-SHA deployed canary before IndexNow notification. A second pre-tag near miss showed that a provider pin can add a new ambient instruction surface without a CLROOM code change: Claude 2.1.278 loaded an external ancestor AGENTS.md through built-in agents-md, so provider-version qualification now includes ambient-input-surface revalidation. Review also found that the first synthetic AGENTS artifact probe could pass on provider version preflight without executing its isolation assertions; v0.4.2 therefore requires an explicit launched-provider execution marker before that evidence can pass. Review of the first Claude AGENTS repair found a second correctness risk: using cwd as the boundary would block legitimate repo-root AGENTS on nested launches. The promoted control therefore binds the clean boundary to the nearest real Git worktree root, with nested-cwd negative and positive evidence at unit, launched-provider and exact-artifact layers. Final review also identified that an absence-only real-TUI confirmation could hide a provider walk that dropped all AGENTS instructions after encountering the denied ambient ancestor. The promoted TUI therefore proves both project instruction retention and external ancestor exclusion in one synthetic nested Git boundary. A local accepted-main qualification then exposed a fixture-level false blocker: the Claude AGENTS probe used a synthetic TMPDIR created under the ambient umask, while CLROOM requires its session projection temp root to be private. The probe now establishes and verifies mode 0700 before launch, and the provider-canary contract owns that fixture invariant. A subsequent accepted-main Codex pre-tag run exposed another release near-miss: the selected codex-app-tools MCP declaration was visible, but its provider-authored absolute launcher paths still targeted the sandbox-denied ambient PluginStore, so the real TUI reported codex_app failed with zero tools. The promoted control now rebases only in-bundle legacy MCP command/cwd paths into the shadow projection, machine-verifies the selected transport paths, and requires the human TUI evidence to confirm a healthy/ready MCP with tools rather than mere server-name visibility.
